record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.context_brief: Roles of FM and AFM spins
record.original_question: What roles do the ferromagnetic spins and the antiferromagnetic spins each play in producing the exchange-bias effect in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?

evidence.quote: iii. What do FM and AFM spins play roles in the EB effect in FM/AFM vdW systems?

artifact.category_tag: Exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a layered heterostructure consisting of a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet (FM) in direct contact with a two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnet (AFM). The system is modeled by a lattice spin Hamiltonian of the form

H = H_FM + H_AFM + H_int,

where H_FM describes intralayer ferromagnetic exchange and anisotropy of the FM layer with spins {S_i^FM}, H_AFM describes intralayer antiferromagnetic exchange and anisotropy of the AFM layer with spins {S_j^AFM} (decomposable into two sublattices with opposite mean magnetization), and H_int = -Σ_{i,j} J_{ij} S_i^FM · S_j^AFM encodes the interfacial coupling across the van der Waals gap. When such a system is cooled in an applied magnetic field through the Néel temperature of the AFM, the hysteresis loop of the FM magnetization becomes shifted along the field axis by an amount H_EB, called the exchange-bias field.

Question: Within this framework, identify and quantitatively characterize the distinct roles played by (a) the ferromagnetic spins {S_i^FM} of the FM layer and (b) the antiferromagnetic spins {S_j^AFM} (including both pinned/uncompensated and rotatable/compensated components) of the AFM layer in producing the exchange-bias shift H_EB. Specifically, determine which microscopic spin configurations — interfacial uncompensated AFM moments, AFM domain walls, FM domain reorganization, or interfacial frustrated FM spins — are responsible for the magnitude, sign, and training behavior of H_EB in FM/AFM van der Waals heterostructures, and provide a predictive relation expressing H_EB in terms of the interfacial couplings J_{ij}, the AFM anisotropy, and the densities of uncompensated interfacial moments.
artifact.status_search_result: The microscopic roles of FM and AFM spins in producing exchange bias in van der Waals FM/AFM heterostructures remain an actively debated open question. Recent experimental and theoretical studies on systems such as Fe3GeTe2/CrSBr, Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, and CrI3-based stacks report competing mechanisms (uncompensated interfacial AFM moments, spin frustration, proximity-induced moments) without a unified predictive theory.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions and perspectives regarding the microscopic origin of EB in vdW FM/AFM systems are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The roles of FM and AFM spins in vdW exchange bias are explicitly listed among the open questions.
